title: The Constitution
note: Drafted for Prompt 12 (Unit 1). Every lesson is a draft until a person reviews it (content/course/README.md).

listen.explanationKey: What is the supreme law of the land?
facts: The U.S. Constitution is the supreme law of the land. No other law can go against it.
It forms the government and says what each part of the government can do.
It also protects the rights of the people.

newWords.meaning: the plan and highest law of a government

story.say: The U.S. Constitution is the supreme law of the land.

help.simpler: The Constitution is the most important law in the United States.
help.example: “Supreme” means highest. The Constitution is the top rule that all other rules must follow.
help.why: The test asks: What is the supreme law of the land? The answer is the Constitution.

story.say: No other law can go against it.

help.simpler: If a law disagrees with the Constitution, the Constitution wins.
help.example: A state cannot make a law that takes away a right the Constitution protects.
help.why: This keeps every law in the country in line with the Constitution.

check.statement: A law can go against the Constitution.

story.say: The Constitution forms the government.

help.simpler: The Constitution sets up the government. It says what parts the government has.
help.example: It creates three branches: Congress, the President and the courts.
help.why: “Forms the government” is one answer to the test question about what the Constitution does.

story.say: It says what each part of the government can do.

help.simpler: The Constitution gives each part of the government its own jobs and limits.
help.example: Congress makes laws. The President carries out laws. The courts explain laws.
help.why: “Defines powers of government” is another answer to what the Constitution does.

story.say: It also protects the rights of the people.

help.simpler: The Constitution keeps people’s rights safe.
help.example: It protects rights like freedom of speech and freedom of religion.
help.why: “Protects the rights of the people” is another answer to what the Constitution does.

check.prompt: Tap the supreme law of the land.

listen.explanationKey: The U.S. Constitution starts with the words “We the People.” What does “We the People” mean?
facts: The Constitution starts with the words “We the People.”
It means the people govern themselves. This is called self-government.
The government gets its power from the people. This is called the consent of the governed.

story.say: The Constitution starts with the words “We the People.”

help.simpler: The first three words of the Constitution are “We the People.”
help.example: The words tell us who made the Constitution: the people of the United States, not a king.
help.why: The test asks what “We the People” means.

story.say: It means the people govern themselves.

help.simpler: The people are in charge of their own country.
help.example: People vote for their leaders, and they can choose new leaders in the next election.
help.why: This idea is at the heart of the Constitution.

story.say: This is called self-government.

help.simpler: “Self-government” means people rule themselves.
help.example: When citizens vote for a mayor, a governor or a President, that is self-government.
help.why: “Self-government” is one answer to what “We the People” means.

check.prompt: What are the first words of the Constitution?

story.say: The government gets its power from the people.

help.simpler: The government has power only because the people agree to give it.
help.example: Leaders get their jobs because people vote for them.
help.why: This shows that the people, not the leaders, are the source of power.

story.say: This is called the consent of the governed.

help.simpler: “Consent” means agreement. “The governed” means the people. So: the people agree to be governed.
help.example: When people vote in an election, they give their consent to the leaders they choose.
help.why: “Consent of the governed” is another answer to what “We the People” means.

check.prompt: Who gives the government its power? Tap them.

listen.explanationKey: How are changes made to the U.S. Constitution?
facts: A change to the Constitution is called an amendment.
Changing the Constitution is hard on purpose. Most of Congress and most of the states must agree.

newWords.meaning: a change or addition to the Constitution

story.say: A change to the Constitution is called an amendment.

help.simpler: An amendment is a change or an addition to the Constitution.
help.example: One amendment gave women the right to vote.
help.why: The test asks how changes are made to the Constitution. The answer is amendments.

story.say: The Constitution has 27 amendments.

help.simpler: The Constitution has been changed 27 times.
help.example: The first ten amendments, added in 1791, are the Bill of Rights.
help.why: The test asks how many amendments the Constitution has. The answer is 27.

check.prompt: How many amendments does the Constitution have?

story.say: Changing the Constitution is hard on purpose.

help.simpler: It is not easy to change the Constitution. That was planned.
help.example: Many ideas for amendments never pass. Only 27 have ever passed.
help.why: Because it is hard to change, the most important rules stay the same over time.

story.say: Most of Congress and most of the states must agree.

help.simpler: Many people must agree: a large part of Congress and a large part of the states.
help.example: Usually two-thirds of Congress votes for it. Then three-fourths of the states must agree.
help.why: This way, one group alone cannot change the Constitution.

readIt.sentence: How many states does the United States have?

writeIt.sentence: The United States has fifty states.

listen.explanationKey: Many documents influenced the U.S. Constitution. Name one.
facts: The people who wrote the Constitution learned from older documents, like the Declaration of Independence, the Articles of Confederation and the Federalist Papers.
George Washington led the meeting that wrote the Constitution in 1787.
The Declaration and the Constitution share big ideas: equality, liberty, natural rights, limited government and self-government.
Tip: for the first question, you only need to name one document. “The Declaration of Independence” is the easiest to remember, because you learn about it in other lessons too.
Tip: for the second question, two short words are enough, like “liberty” and “equality.”

newWords.meaning: to help shape how something turns out
being treated the same as everyone else
a government whose power has limits

story.say: The people who wrote the Constitution learned from older documents.

help.simpler: The writers of the Constitution used ideas from documents written before.
help.example: Like a cook who learns from older recipes, they kept the best ideas.
help.why: The test asks you to name one document that influenced the Constitution.

story.say: They learned from the Declaration of Independence, the Articles of Confederation and the Federalist Papers.

help.simpler: Three of these older documents are the Declaration, the Articles of Confederation and the Federalist Papers.
help.example: The Articles of Confederation were the country’s first plan of government, before the Constitution.
help.why: Any one of these is a correct answer to the test question. You only need to name one.

story.say: George Washington led the meeting that wrote the Constitution in 1787.

help.simpler: In 1787, leaders met in Philadelphia to write the Constitution. George Washington led the meeting.
help.example: This meeting is called the Constitutional Convention.
help.why: George Washington later became the first President. He is in other test questions too.

check.prompt: Who led the meeting that wrote the Constitution?

story.say: The Declaration and the Constitution share big ideas.

help.simpler: Both documents are built on the same important ideas.
help.example: One idea, equality, means every person should be treated the same under the law.
help.why: The test asks you to name two of these ideas.

story.say: They are equality, liberty, natural rights, limited government and self-government.

help.simpler: Equality, liberty, natural rights, limited government and self-government are the big ideas.
help.example: Limited government means the government has limits. It cannot do whatever it wants.
help.why: Name any two of these on the test, for example “liberty” and “equality.”

check.statement: Liberty and equality are ideas from the Declaration and the Constitution.

story.say: Tip: if asked to name one document, “the Declaration of Independence” is the easiest to remember.

help.simpler: If the officer asks for one document, you can say “the Declaration of Independence.”
help.example: Officer: “Name one document that influenced the Constitution.” You: “The Declaration of Independence.”
help.why: You already know this document from other lessons, so it is easy to remember.

story.say: Tip: if asked for two important ideas, two short words are enough, like “liberty” and “equality.”

help.simpler: For two important ideas, you can just say “liberty and equality.”
help.example: Officer: “Name two important ideas from the Declaration and the Constitution.” You: “Liberty and equality.”
help.why: Short answers are fine on the test, as long as they are correct.

check.prompt: Which one is a document that influenced the Constitution?

readIt.sentence: Who is the Father of Our Country?

writeIt.sentence: Washington is the Father of Our Country.
